ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows three different placements of the same decision die. On the left die, the visible top face is “no”, and the two adjacent side faces are both “YES”. On the middle die, two adjacent faces are visible as “YES”, and another visible side face is “maybe”. On the right die, the visible top face is “no”, one side face is “YES”, and another side face is “no”. Reasoning: Take the face whose top face is “no” as the anchor, and compare the left and right views that both have the same top face “no”. They show the four side faces adjacent around this top face: among them, three faces are labeled “YES”, and one face is labeled “no”. The “maybe” face appearing in the middle view is not among these four side faces around the top face “no”, so it is the sixth face opposite to that top face “no”. Thus the die has a total of 6 faces, of which 3 are “YES”. So the probability of getting “YES” in one roll is 3/6 = 1/2.

raw_record.question_text: In the diagram, one can see my decision-die in three different positions. What is the probability I get a "YES" when rolling this die once?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the left cube position shows a top face labeled "no" and two adjacent side faces labeled "YES"; the middle position shows two adjacent faces labeled "YES" and a third face labeled "maybe"; the right position shows a top face labeled "no", one side labeled "YES", and one side labeled "no". Use the top-"no" face as an anchor and compare the cyclic order/orientation of the side faces around it in the first and third positions. These two anchored views reveal the four faces around that top face: three are "YES" and one is "no". Then use the middle view to identify the remaining face, opposite the anchored top "no", as "maybe". Therefore the die has 3 YES faces out of 6 faces, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.
